headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network defaults make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible between LangGraph and Windsurf.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can read/write application files and uses developer-defined tools, while Windsurf exposes workspace files, clipboard, and MCP servers. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if one agent writes attacker-controlled text that the other later parses. The interaction is documented only at the profile level, so uncertainty stays medium rather than low.
conditions: IF LangGraph writes untrusted content into shared workspace files that Windsurf later opens
IF Windsurf ingests file or clipboard content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable clipboard-based handoff
Require provenance tags on inter-agent files
Review any shared MCP server allowlist
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing wrappers before cross-agent file reads

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph handles model provider API keys and broad network egress, while Windsurf reads workspace files and also has broad egress plus MCP access. If they share files or a workspace, sensitive code or secrets touched by LangGraph can flow into Windsurf outputs or remote calls. The shared-workspace path is plausible from the profiles, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or checkpointer-backed state
IF LangGraph stores secrets or sensitive graph state in files that Windsurf can read
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared files
Use separate OS users or containers
Restrict Windsurf to read-only on shared paths
Rotate any exposed API keys
requires-engineering: encrypt shared state at rest with per-agent keys

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph can write filesystem state and persists shared state via a checkpointer store, while Windsurf can write files, modify git state, and supports multiple instances via the local filesystem. Both therefore have overlapping write authority over mutable resources, and the profiles do not show locking or coordination. That makes destructive conflicts and lost updates likely in default use.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or repository
IF LangGraph checkpointer state and Windsurf workspace state are stored on the same filesystem without locks
mitigations: Use separate repos or directories
Turn on file locking for shared state
Disable Windsurf auto-commit or auto-edit on shared paths
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around the checkpointer and workspace

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph is an orchestration framework that can emit node outputs, and Windsurf is a coding agent that can act on workspace context and modify files or git state. If Windsurf treats LangGraph output as authoritative, a mistaken or injected intermediate result can cascade into code changes or commits. No verification mechanism is shown in either profile, so the default pathway is dangerous.
conditions: IF Windsurf consumes LangGraph-produced text or artifacts as trusted task input
IF Windsurf applies edits or commits without an independent verification step
mitigations: Insert a human review gate before edits
Require schema validation on LangGraph outputs
Keep LangGraph outputs read-only until checked
Disable auto-apply for generated patches
requires-engineering: add deterministic verification between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not declare regulated-data certifications or residency constraints, so a concrete compliance breach cannot be proven. The only clear issue is that LangGraph handles model provider API keys and Windsurf handles workspace code/files, which could matter if regulated data is placed there. Because the missing compliance metadata is on both agents, the risk remains low and uncertain.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace
IF one agent is later configured with a residency or retention policy not matched by the other
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared files
Document retention settings for both tools
Use separate tenants or accounts
Review vendor compliance docs before deployment
requires-engineering: enforce policy-based routing and retention controls
